stereo share. Section 2 cited it as 'fetched 2026-10-15' but no artifact
recorded the fetch or its contents, and stt-concurrency had already recorded

the_finding_that_matters_more_multi_acco._note: verbatim quotes from the fetched page, in Deepgram's own words

verbatim.per_project: Rate limits apply per project, not per account or API key. Creating additional projects under the same account will not grant you additional concurrency. Secondary projects created on a self-serve account are limited to a single concurrent stream by design. Bypassing rate limits by spreading traffic across multiple projects violates our Terms of Service.
verbatim.scaling: Rate limits are scoped to a project. One customer maps to one project for the purposes of these limits. Multiple API keys inside a single project all draw from that project's concurrency pool. Adding more projects under the same account does not increase the concurrency available to you.
verbatim.what_not_to_do: Do not create additional projects, additional accounts, or otherwise distribute traffic across projects to work around per-project limits. These setups are detected. Secondary projects on a self-serve account are restricted to 1 concurrent stream, and bypassing rate limits this way violates our Terms of Service.
verbatim.fix_if_hitting_limits: Consolidate your traffic into a single project, then contact sales about moving to a Growth or Enterprise agreement with a higher concurrency allocation.

consequence_for_the_plan: The operator's hypothesis - split the corpus in half across two accounts to
double throughput - is not merely a ToS grey area. The page names it under
'What not to do', says the setups are DETECTED, and states that secondary
projects on a self-serve account are throttled to ONE concurrent stream.
That last clause is decisive and was not previously known: a second
self-serve project does not merely fail to help, it is capped at 1 concurrent
stream. The throughput hypothesis would not have been slower - it would have
been 25x WORSE, because the carrier request would have had to run alone.
The plan's existing rule is CONFIRMED and now sourced rather than inferred:
the second key is A WALLET, NOT A WORKER. Sequential failover on 402 only,
never concurrent. Two keys inside ONE project draw from the SAME concurrency
pool, which is why a second key adds budget and zero throughput.
